description: Fix ceiling collision, stairs geometry/climbing, and hands wall-clipping. All three are physics/geometry fixes in the same game loop.
steps: STEP 1 - Ceiling collision: In src/game/FirstPersonController.ts, in the updateStep() method, add a HEAD/ceiling collision check BEFORE the ground landing logic. After applying vertical velocity (this.camera.position.y += this.velocity.y * delta), iterate through colliders to check if the player's head (camera.position.y + 0.2) has entered a collider from below. If the player's head box overlaps a collider AND the previous frame head was below that collider's min.y, clamp camera.position.y so head stays below collider.min.y and set velocity.y = 0. This prevents jumping through ceiling panels. The check should look like: for each collider, if player is horizontally overlapping AND (camera.position.y + 0.2) > collider.min.y AND (prevHeadY) <= collider.min.y AND collider.min.y > feetY + 0.5 (to not trigger on step-up obstacles), then clamp.

STEP 2 - Stairs geometry fix: In src/editor/EditorObjects.ts, in the stairs_straight object (around line 2871), fix the gaps between steps. Currently each step has a tread at (0, sy+0.5, sz) with depth 0.52 and a riser at (0, sy+0.25, sz+0.23) with depth 0.06. The gap between the back of one tread and the next riser needs to be filled. Add a fill box for each step (except step 0) that covers the gap between the previous tread's back edge and the current riser's front face: box(2, 0.5, gapDepth, M.conc3) positioned to fill the void under each tread. The gap is from the back of tread (sz+0.26) to the front of the riser of the next step going forward. Actually re-examine: the treads center at sz (which is -i*0.5), depth 0.52, so back edge is sz-0.26, front edge is sz+0.26. The riser is at sz+0.23, depth 0.06, so back edge riser is sz+0.20, front edge riser is sz+0.26. So riser connects flush to tread front. The BOTTOM of the staircase (between steps looking from under) has a gap. To close it, add a solid fill panel that covers the underside: for each step i>0, add a box that fills from the previous step's tread back edge to the current step's riser. This gap is: previous tread back = (-(i-1)*0.5) - 0.26, current riser front = (-i*0.5) + 0.26. So gap = 0. Actually there IS no gap in the front-back direction between riser and tread of the same step. The issue is likely the SIDE WALLS being too tall, creating colliders that block the player from entering the stair area. Fix the side walls: instead of tall growing boxes that create large colliders blocking entry, make them only extend slightly above each step level (e.g., 0.5 units above each step top, like a handrail height). OR better: change the side wall construction to use stair-following segments that each have height = 0.52 (matching step height + margin) so they don't create tall blocking colliders. Change from: box(0.06, h, 0.52, M.concDirty) with h = 0.56 + i*0.5 at y = h/2, to: box(0.06, 0.62, 0.52, M.concDirty) at y = sy + 0.31 for each step, so each side wall segment is only 0.62 tall (just above the step height of 0.5, within step-up range). This way the colliders from side walls are never taller than stepUpHeight.

STEP 3 - Stairs fill the underside gaps: Add a solid angled fill panel beneath the stairs to close the visible gaps from below. Add a large triangular-fill using a box that covers the entire staircase underside: box(2, 0.1, 4.16, M.conc3) angled to match the stair slope. Position at center of stair run, rotated to match the ~45-degree angle of the stairs. This closes the visual gap without affecting step-up collision.

STEP 4 - Hands wall retraction: In src/game/Hands.ts, add a wall proximity system. Add a new method setWallProximity(distance: number) that accepts the distance to the nearest wall in front of the player. In the update() method, after computing final hand positions, if wall distance < 0.5 (the hands forward extent), retract both arms' z-position proportionally: retractZ = Math.max(0, 0.5 - distance) * 0.8. Apply this retraction to both leftArm.position.z and rightArm.position.z (add retractZ to pull them back, since negative z is forward). Also slightly raise the hands (y += retractZ * 0.3) and tilt them back (rotation.x += retractZ * 0.5) for a natural look of hands being pulled back when near a wall.

STEP 5 - Wall proximity raycasting: In src/editor/PlaytestMode.ts, in the animate/update loop, add a forward raycast from the camera position in the camera's forward direction. Use the existing this.raycaster. Cast against the scene meshes with a max distance of 0.7. Pass the hit distance to this.hands.setWallProximity(distance). If no hit, pass 999. This raycast should happen every frame before hands.update().
STEP 6 - Build verification: Run npm install && npm run build in the project directory to confirm everything compiles cleanly.
acceptance_criteria: npm run build completes without TypeScript errors
FirstPersonController.ts contains ceiling collision logic that prevents upward movement through colliders
EditorObjects.ts stairs_straight has side walls that don't create colliders taller than 0.55 units above each step
EditorObjects.ts stairs_straight has filled underside geometry
Hands.ts has a setWallProximity method that retracts hands when near walls
PlaytestMode.ts has a forward raycast that feeds wall distance to the Hands system

findings: All three fixes implemented and build passes cleanly. The box() helper in EditorObjects.ts returns THREE.Mesh which allows direct position/rotation manipulation for the underside fill panel. The raycaster in PlaytestMode.ts was already declared as a class property so no additional setup was needed.
